title: Chinese Five-Spice Powder

ingredients.title: Spice Blend
items: 1 small piece Chinese cinnamon (cassia), broken into pieces

instruction.title: Toast the Spices
steps: Place Sichuan peppercorns, fennel seeds, star anise, cloves, and cassia cinnamon in a dry skillet.
Toast the spices over low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant.
Remove from the heat and allow the spices to cool completely.

instruction.title: Grind the Spices
steps: Transfer the cooled spices to a spice grinder or clean coffee grinder.
Grind until the mixture becomes a fine powder.
Sift the powder if a smoother texture is desired.

instruction.title: Store
steps: Transfer the five-spice powder to an airtight, dry container.
Store in a cool, dark place away from direct sunlight.
Use within a few months for the best aroma and flavor.

chefTips: Toast the whole spices gently to release their natural oils and deepen the flavor.
Use Chinese cinnamon (cassia) rather than regular sweet cinnamon for a more traditional flavor.
Adjust the Sichuan peppercorns or cloves slightly if you prefer a milder blend.
A small amount goes a long way because five-spice powder has a strong, concentrated aroma.
Use it to season roasted meats, marinades, stir-fries, braises, vegetables, and tofu.
